pr_title: Avoid throwing exceptions on DrawableRuleset load interruption
pr_comments:
You have to consider the possible repercussions from exiting rather than throwing - throwing will interrupt the entire load async call, up to the point it started. Exiting will not do this.

I don’t like this on that principle.

The mentioned issue is a debugger exception. It is irrelevant, the user should ignore exceptions they don’t want.

Can you explain how the repercussions would affect us in this case? I checked the complete flow and it looks safe. I was trying to find best practices for this, since this is a case we are 100% in control of the async flow (*we* are the call site).

I'm all for avoiding throwing exceptions we don't need to. For the issue you mention to affect us, it would mean that the framework loading was unaware of the cancellation token's presence, which I think we are guaranteed to not be the case?

On further discussion it seems safest to throw here after all. Reasoning is that `DrawableRuleset` is not sealed – a custom ruleset could be doing more execution in the BDL method which would continue to run. By throwing an exception we can be sure we exit as early as possible.

issue_context.title: OperationCancelledException when exiting gameplay
issue_context.body:
**Describe the crash:** 
Sometimes when exiting from gameplay to the song select screen while debugging, the game will throw the following exception:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/27722894/74062809-63499700-49ef-11ea-8274-c3f7b0356729.png)

Game works fine after resuming in the IDE and this is not visible in logs, but I think it's still not something that should be happening

**osu!lazer version:** 
latest master as of 07/02
comments:
Where is this caught? There are a few places that catch `OperationCanceled`.

It might just be that the throw is the sanest way to cancel the operation by unwinding the stack, not sure.
What would be the easiest way to check that?

Well, you should be able to just keep stepping out of the exception throw site until you hit a `catch`. VS also has an event log that shows where exceptions are caught and rethrown but I can see you're on ~~Rider~~ VS Code, not sure if it has an equivalent.
What IDE are you using? Please turn off "break on user handled" mode.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35318437/74076755-34232d80-49cf-11ea-8b5c-ee0dc9eaadda.png)

Based on what was said on discord and the image shown, probably VSCode. Unchecking this works.
Actually this is quite well spotted and something we *can* avoid. Will PR a change to avoid exception usage.

review_comments: have you tried this? i think you'll find there is.
I only looked at the code, my bad if that's correct

2 points:
- For this expression that results in `bool?`, `== true` is meaningful.
- But the usage of `CancellationToken?` is unnecessary.  `CancellationToken.None` and `default(CancellationToken)` both mean "will never be canceled", and widely used in BCL.

I'll send a PR for this.
You're welcome to look into that, but I believe it is nullable for a reason (to do with DI).
